question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck sign and no lights or gates?
options: a:Only cross when directed by a flagger,b:Assume no train is coming and proceed at normal speed,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming
note: Always approach such crossings cautiously, look and listen for trains, and cross only when it is safe.

question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen,b:Drive around a lowered gate,c:Speed up to beat the train
note: Always approach crossings with caution: look both ways, listen, and be prepared to stop for trains or for vehicles using the rails.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other road users allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles,b:The decreased noise of larger vehicles,c:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles
note: Large vehicles require greater stopping distances; smaller vehicle drivers should leave space and avoid blind spots.

question: What are the standard colors for most warning signs that alert you to hazards ahead?
options: a:Black letters on a white background,b:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background,c:White symbols on a blue background
note: Most warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering; work zone warnings are usually orange with black markings.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may turn in the arrow's direction without yielding,b:The arrow is not used as a traffic signal,c:Same as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop or clear the intersection
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected-turn phase is ending; slow and prepare to stop as you would for a circular yellow light.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what is a driver's obligation?
options: a:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to the right-of-way,b:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them,c:Require pedestrians to always yield to vehicles
note: Drivers must be alert to pedestrians and yield right-of-way to them to prevent collisions, even if pedestrians are not crossing legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:You may pass with caution,b:You may not pass from your lane,c:You must slow down immediately
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane indicates passing is prohibited in your direction.

question: If you observe other drivers acting angrily, how should you respond?
options: a:React with hand gestures to de-escalate,b:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid eye contact or provoking gestures,c:Make eye contact to calm them down
note: Physically and mentally distance yourself, avoid eye contact and gestures, and take actions to get out of potential danger safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to a steady yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely,b:Speed up to beat the light,c:Ignore it because green just ended
note: When you see a steady yellow, prepare to stop; if you are too close to stop safely, proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection require drivers to do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way; be prepared to stop if necessary,b:Always come to a full stop regardless of conditions,c:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly
note: A red-and-white downward-pointing triangular sign is a yield sign; reduce speed, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and stop if required.

question: If you are involved in a traffic accident, what is your immediate responsibility?
options: a:Stop immediately and provide assistance if needed,b:Drive away if the accident seems minor,c:Continue on and report it later
note: Stop immediately, render aid as appropriate, call police or emergency services if needed, and exchange information as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a two-way left-turn center lane, which maneuver is permitted?
options: a:Making left turns from either direction into or out of the lane,b:Continuing straight through the intersection in that lane,c:Passing slower traffic
note: A two-way center turn lane is reserved for left turns from either direction (and in many areas for U-turns where legal), not for passing or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions,c:A recommended safe speed under all conditions
note: A speed limit sign indicates the maximum legal speed for the road under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions are unsafe.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:New drivers,c:Human error
note: Most crashes occur due to human error — mistakes such as inattention, misjudgment, and poor decision making.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do regarding the injured person?
options: a:Leave the injured where they are and do not provide any assistance,b:Always move injured people away from the scene immediately,c:Do not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained
note: Do not move injured people unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid if you are able and it's necessary, while waiting for skilled help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is never permitted,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction,c:Vehicles in either direction may pass when it is safe to do so
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is allowed when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the hand signal of a driver's left arm and hand extended upward indicate?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right,b:The driver intends to stop,c:The driver intends to turn left
note: When the left arm is raised upward, the driver is signaling a right turn using hand signals.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are and wait,b:Slowly proceed and allow the vehicle to pass,c:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop
note: On a two-lane or undivided highway, immediately drive as near as possible to the right edge and stop to yield to an emergency vehicle, avoiding stopping in an intersection.

question: Before you turn the ignition on, what should you do about seat belts?
options: a:Only ensure child passengers are belted,b:Only ensure adult passengers are belted,c:Make sure you and all passengers are properly buckled
note: Develop a routine: buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are properly restrained before starting the vehicle.

question: When driving in fog, which actions should you take?
options: a:Speed up to clear the fog quickly,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead,c:Use low-beam headlights
note: In fog, do not use high beams (they worsen visibility). Use low beams, slow down, and proceed with caution.

question: What type of highway signs must drivers obey because they indicate required actions?
options: a:Regulatory signs,b:Warning signs,c:Information signs
note: Regulatory signs indicate laws or requirements (speed limits, no turn signs) and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center two-way left-turn lane, which maneuver is allowed?
options: a:Making left turns into or out of the lane,b:Passing slower traffic,c:Driving straight through the intersection
note: Center two-way left-turn lanes are reserved for left turns or legal U-turns where permitted; they are not for passing or through travel.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it begins to rain,b:You should reduce following distance while braking,c:Wet roads never affect stopping distance
note: Road surfaces can be most slippery at the start of a rainfall; reduce speed and increase following distance to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop even if the road is clear,b:Only yield to traffic on your left,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you are entering
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection; stop only if necessary.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery?
options: a:Drive faster to get through the slippery patch quicker,b:Slow down and use extra caution,c:Maintain the posted speed limit even if conditions are poor
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of wet, snowy, or icy conditions and increase following distance to maintain control.

question: How should you scan the road ahead to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Continually scan the road and roadsides for potential hazards,b:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake,c:Stare straight ahead at all times
note: Search and identify potential problems early by scanning the entire roadway and both shoulders frequently.

question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:Only when other vehicles yield first,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren
note: Yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights by pulling over and stopping as necessary.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby,b:Speed up to cross before a train arrives,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates
note: A railroad warning sign indicates a potential train crossing; always be prepared to stop and obey gates and signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you turn right on a red light?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and if no sign prohibits the turn,b:Before coming to a complete stop,c:Only if pedestrians have not started to cross the intersecting crosswalk
note: You may turn right on red only after you make a full stop and if signs do not prohibit the turn; always yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space required to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic,b:Only whether you used your turn signal,c:Only whether there is a stop sign
note: You need adequate space to cross, and that space depends on roadway conditions, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the left,b:The vehicle whose driver honks first,c:The vehicle approaching from the right
note: At intersections of similar roads without traffic control devices, yield to vehicles approaching from the right.

question: Which action can cause a license suspension related to impaired driving enforcement?
options: a:Not switching off high beams near another vehicle,b:Driving 10 mph over the posted speed limit,c:Refusing to submit to a requested chemical test
note: Refusing a chemical test when arrested for Operating a Vehicle While Impaired (OVI) can result in a one- to five-year administrative license suspension in addition to other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas,b:When you are in a construction zone,c:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic
note: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you impede traffic flow; drive at a safe speed consistent with conditions and the posted limits.

question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic accidents?
options: a:Newer vehicles,b:Inattentive driving,c:Driving only on unfamiliar roads
note: Being inattentive is a frequent cause of crashes. Speeding and following too closely are also common contributing factors.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:In a tunnel,b:Only on a crosswalk,c:Only on a highway bridge
note: Parking is not allowed on crosswalks, bridges, or inside tunnels; park only where it is legal and visible to other drivers.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and walk to the rear of the vehicle to be sure the way is clear,b:Sound your horn to warn children and then back up,c:Rely only on your mirrors to check behind you
note: When children are present, exit the vehicle and visually confirm the area behind it before backing out.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important in winter,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe
note: Do not use cruise control in snow, ice, or similar hazardous conditions; winter driving requires extra precautions and vehicle checks.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are a law enforcement officer,b:They are likely blind and may not see or hear your vehicle,c:They are deaf and cannot hear approaching cars
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a pedestrian is blind; you must slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop to prevent injury.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels drift off the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately brake hard and stop,b:Take your foot off the accelerator,c:Accelerate and quickly steer back onto the road
note: Do not panic; reduce speed by easing off the accelerator, regain control, check traffic, then gradually steer back onto the pavement.

question: About how fast does the average body metabolize alcohol?
options: a:About two drinks per hour,b:About three drinks per hour,c:About one standard drink per hour
note: On average, the body processes roughly one standard drink each hour; factors such as weight and food intake can change this rate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but lacking a stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down and verifying there is no cross traffic,b:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection,c:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe to proceed
note: Stop before entering the intersection when a stop sign is present (even if there's no stop line or crosswalk) and proceed only when safe.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light indicate?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears,b:Proceed slowly through the intersection,c:Stop
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears unless signage indicates otherwise.

question: Which factor most affects your ability to stop your vehicle safely?
options: a:The time of day,b:Signal lights,c:Road conditions such as wet or icy surfaces
note: Stopping distance is greatly affected by road surface condition, visibility, vehicle speed, and brake/tire condition.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle with flashing lights to pass?
options: a:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction,b:Only if it is following you from behind,c:Pull over to the right edge and stop regardless of the vehicle's direction of approach
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, no matter its direction of approach.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Lie down in the car and go to sleep,b:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help,c:Get out of the car and walk for help
note: Staying in your car improves the chance of being located and provides shelter; leave only if you know exactly where help is and it's safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How is a speed limit defined?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions,b:The exact speed required to avoid a ticket under any condition,c:The suggested safe speed for all conditions
note: A speed limit is the legal maximum or minimum speed under ideal conditions; you may need to drive slower when conditions are unsafe.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit,c:Turn your flashers on and continue driving
note: On a one-way street, if an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign with a black symbol typically indicate?
options: a:Directions to cities and towns ahead,b:Traffic laws and regulatory rules,c:Warning about conditions or hazards ahead
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols are warning signs that alert drivers to conditions or hazards on or near the road ahead.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed,b:Slow down and remain in your lane,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop
note: Immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling over to the curb or roadside and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver behind you signals to pass, how should you help them complete the pass?
options: a:Maintain the same speed,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing,c:Slow down to provide space in front of your vehicle so they can re-enter the lane
note: Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle and allow the passing driver to move back into the lane safely.

question: What are the colors used for highway signs that show distances or destinations (like the next exit)?
options: a:Red background with white letters,b:Yellow background with black letters,c:Green background with white letters and symbols
note: Destination and distance signs are typically green with white lettering or symbols.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow the rider?
options: a:To use the bicycle lane,b:Only half a lane,c:Use of a full traffic lane — the motorcycle is entitled to the same lane width as other vehicles
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and must be given full lane width and safe following distance.

question: What minimum following 'safety zone' should motorists leave behind a motorcyclist?
options: a:At least three seconds,b:Two seconds,c:One second
note: Leave a safety zone of at least three seconds behind motorcycles; small contact can cause serious injury to riders.

question: On roads without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic,b:The same side as vehicle traffic is moving,c:The side of the road facing oncoming traffic
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and react if necessary.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
options: a:20 feet,b:35 feet,c:30 feet
note: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk so pedestrians and other drivers can clearly see the stopped vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually the best practice?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights until safely merged,b:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening without accelerating,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge smoothly
note: Accelerate on the entrance ramp to match the speed of traffic and merge safely; traffic already on the freeway has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, what's the safest relative speed to maintain?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limit,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to avoid collisions,c:Drive slower than surrounding traffic to be safe
note: Crashes often happen when drivers travel much faster or slower than surrounding traffic; maintain the flow while obeying speed limits.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck carrying flammable liquids, what should you be prepared for at railroad crossings?
options: a:Pass the bus or truck if it stops,b:Be prepared to stop at railroad crossings,c:Increase your following distance but not stop
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids are required to stop at railroad crossings; be ready to stop when following them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is attempting to pass your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road immediately,b:Signal them when it's safe for them to pass,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust speed to allow safe passing
note: Maintain your lane, check for oncoming traffic, and adjust your speed to make it easier for the passing vehicle to return to the lane safely.

question: What should you do when confronted by an aggressive driver?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down,b:Avoid eye contact,c:Retaliate by tailgating them
note: Remain calm, avoid engaging the aggressive driver, and increase the distance between you and them. Do not make eye contact or respond with gestures.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children,b:Always stop whether or not a sign or stop is present,c:Watch for children and be prepared to stop
note: Be alert for children near school crossings and be ready to stop; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: May you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if you look carefully in both directions first,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate,c:Never; wait until the gates are fully raised and lights/bells have stopped
note: If lights are flashing, gates are lowered, or bells are sounding at a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop and do not drive around or under moving gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Any lane because the street is one-way,b:The lane closest to your previous lane (the nearest lane to the left),c:The rightmost lane
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from unless lane markings indicate otherwise.

question: What is an important action to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Only drive on back roads to avoid traffic,b:Ignore other drivers because they should watch you,c:Communicate your intentions to other road users (signals
note: Use turn signals, brake lights, and other communication to make your intentions clear and help prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is street or drag racing on public roads acceptable?
options: a:Only during clear weather conditions,b:Only at night when traffic is light,c:Never — it is illegal
note: Street racing on public roads is illegal and extremely dangerous; it can cause serious injury or death and carries severe penalties.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, liquor) change how alcohol affects reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Yes — beer impairs you less than wine,b:No — effects depend on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream,c:Yes — wine impairs you less than mixed drinks
note: All types of alcohol impair reflexes and judgment; impairment depends on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass and the cyclist may swerve to avoid hazards,b:A bicycle always has the right-of-way in every situation,c:Cyclists cannot hear motor vehicles
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid obstacles and drivers may be hidden from oncoming traffic when passing; give extra space and caution.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line between lanes?
options: a:Only during daylight hours,b:When it is safe to change lanes,c:At any time regardless of conditions
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off the highways as quickly as possible,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance
note: Reducing speed and increasing following distance are key to avoiding crashes on snow- or ice-covered roads.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Yield to other traffic and be prepared to stop if necessary,b:School zones,c:Construction zones
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs, indicating you must slow and yield the right-of-way.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a symbol indicate?
options: a:That some drivers must yield to others,b:The specified action shown is forbidden,c:That drivers must come to a complete stop
note: A red circle with a slash across a black symbol indicates the action depicted is prohibited by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs,b:Only at stop signs,c:Only when a police officer orders you to stop
note: You must stop at stop signs, red or flashing red lights, and any time a traffic officer directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to pedestrians,b:Only to vehicles on your right,c:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic as well as to pedestrians, bicyclists, and others already in the intersection.

question: If an oncoming driver is heading into your lane, what immediate actions should you take?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid the collision,b:Steer left into the oncoming lane,c:Blow your horn
note: Honk to attract attention, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly; avoid swerving left into oncoming traffic unless absolutely necessary.

question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what does it mean?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:Come to a complete stop before turning,c:Merge into the lane in the arrow's direction without yielding
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked by two solid yellow lines dividing traffic, when may you cross them?
options: a:To pass slower vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic,b:Under no circumstances ever,c:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited
note: A broken yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is allowed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close should your wheels be to the curb when parallel parking?
options: a:Within 10 inches of the curb,b:Within 18 inches of the curb,c:Within 12 inches of the curb
note: When parallel parking, position your wheels within 12 inches of the curb and park only where it is safe and legal.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Only turn off the engine,b:Lock the ignition,c:Only set the parking brake
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, take the key, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light for your lane, what must you do before turning?
options: a:You still have the absolute right-of-way to turn without yielding,b:You may no longer turn in that direction,c:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, you may turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: During normal weather and traffic conditions, what is the recommended minimum following distance?
options: a:One second,b:Three seconds,c:Two seconds
note: Keep a minimum three-second following distance in normal conditions and increase it when conditions worsen.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment and cause poisoning,b:It causes a loss of hearing,c:It reduces fuel efficiency only
note: A leaking exhaust can permit dangerous carbon monoxide fumes to enter the vehicle interior, posing a potentially fatal risk.

question: What is the best immediate action to avoid hydroplaning on wet or slushy roads?
options: a:Watch for standing water or puddles,b:Keep tires properly maintained,c:Reduce your speed when roads are wet
note: Reduce speed and drive cautiously when roads are wet; also avoid cruise control in wet or icy conditions and maintain good tires.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You might not see the road between the cars,b:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals,c:You might not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping distance and is a leading cause of rear-end collisions.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign mean at a given location?
options: a:You may never stop there under any circumstance,b:You may stop only briefly to load or discharge passengers,c:You may park if the driver remains in the vehicle
note: A 'No standing' sign permits temporary stops to pick up or discharge passengers only; parking or leaving the vehicle is not allowed.

question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit,b:Maintain a constant speed regardless of the curve,c:Slow down before entering the curve and gradually accelerate as you exit
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and gradually increase speed after you have cleared it to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, railroad crossing, or intersection may you legally pass?
options: a:You may not pass within 200 feet of such locations,b:You may not pass within 500 feet of such locations,c:You may not pass within 100 feet of such locations
note: Drivers may not pass other vehicles within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, railroad crossing, or intersection.

question: Which effects does alcohol have on driving ability?
options: a:Only loss of concentration,b:Only slower judgment,c:Loss of concentration
note: Alcohol impairs multiple mental and physical functions needed for safe driving, including vision, judgment, coordination, and concentration.

question: Which of the following describes a diamond-shaped sign?
options: a:A road hazard/warning sign,b:A school crossing sign,c:An interstate route sign
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs indicating hazardous locations or areas where special rules apply.

question: If a vehicle approaches with high beams that are blinding you, what is the safest response?
options: a:Flash your lights repeatedly at the other driver,b:Keep using your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs,c:Look toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes
note: Avoid being blinded by looking slightly to the right edge of the road and allowing your eyes to adjust until the vehicle passes.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait until the police arrive at the scene before leaving,b:Leave a written note with your name,c:Do nothing and drive away once you have left contact information for the police
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, stop and try to find the owner; if you can't, leave a written notice with your information and the circumstances.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you focus your vision?
options: a:Toward the right edge of the road ahead rather than directly at headlights,b:Over your shoulder,c:Directly at the oncoming headlights
note: If oncoming drivers fail to dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road ahead to avoid being blinded by glare.

question: Is holding a pet on your lap while driving safe or legal?
options: a:It is always legal if the animal is asleep,b:No — it is dangerous and may be illegal because it distracts the driver,c:It is safe if you are an experienced driver
note: Holding an animal while driving is distracting and may lead to moving violation charges in addition to causing an unsafe driving condition.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service area,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Slam on your brakes immediately
note: Grip the wheel, avoid hard braking, gradually slow, and steer to a safe area before stopping if you experience a blowout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Honk to warn pedestrians and drivers,b:Drive slowly so others can move out of your way,c:Stop and go only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line but not from the lane next to the solid line,b:Passing is permitted from either direction,c:Passing is permitted only at night
note: When a broken yellow line is adjacent to a solid yellow line, traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe; the traffic next to the solid line may not.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Use your horn to warn or scare it away,b:Take no special action,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible
note: Be very cautious when animals are on or near the road. When possible, warn them or other drivers and pass slowly; do not pass too closely or act unpredictably.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes to the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Just use your side mirror without signaling,b:Only look in your rearview mirror,c:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot
note: Check mirrors, look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot, signal, and then change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes — if no oncoming traffic,b:Yes,c:No — you may not pass across double solid yellow lines
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited in both directions except to turn into or out of a driveway or private road.

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The time of day,b:The condition of your vehicle's brakes,c:Your reaction time
note: Stopping distance depends on factors like reaction time, vehicle weight, brake and tire condition, road surface, and speed — not simply the time of day.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Turn right or left because the road ahead is closed,b:Slow down and proceed with care,c:Come to a full stop and proceed only when the way is clear
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, then proceed when safe.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic,c:Stop
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop and proceeding only when safe, similar to a stop sign.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to smaller ones?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots,b:Larger vehicles have no blind spots,c:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots
note: The bigger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots; avoid lingering in those areas and position your vehicle where the truck driver can see you.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic crossing an unprotected railroad track, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and need not check for trains,b:There is enough space to get completely across the tracks without stopping,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks
note: Before driving onto tracks, make sure you can clear them completely; never stop on the tracks or attempt to pass another vehicle while crossing.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light,b:Continue normally through the intersection without slowing,c:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow light means 'caution' — slow down, look, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: What lane entitlement does a motorcycle have?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles,b:The bicycle lane only,c:Half the width of a lane
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like other vehicles and need space to maneuver safely.

question: What should you do when approaching an intersection showing a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed,b:Come to a complete stop and wait for it to change,c:Proceed through the intersection slowly and with caution
note: A flashing yellow light means 'caution' — slow down, look, and proceed with care while scanning traffic both ways.

question: At night when another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam setting,b:Low beam setting,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights
note: Use low beams when approaching or following another vehicle at night to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice regarding crossing when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Enter crosswalks at any time because drivers must stop,b:Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching,c:Always insist on the right-of-way over cars
note: Even though pedestrians often have the right-of-way, only cross when it is safe; an approaching vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before turning should you signal?
options: a:50 feet before the turn,b:20 feet before the turn,c:At least 100 feet before the turn
note: Signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes to notify other drivers of your intentions.

question: When a school bus stops to unload children on a highway with four or more lanes, when must drivers stop?
options: a:Drivers on the opposite side of the highway must always stop,b:Only if they are traveling in the same direction as the bus,c:Only if children are crossing in front of the bus
note: On roadways with four or more lanes, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the stopped school bus is required to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging Traffic' sign on the freeway, how should you react?
options: a:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them,b:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe,c:Always remain at your current speed
note: On multi-lane roads, move over one lane if safe to make room for merging vehicles; be courteous and alert.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Whenever you are changing lanes,b:Only when turning left,c:Only when pulling toward a curb
note: Look over your shoulder to check blind spots every time you change lanes, turn, or pull toward or away from a curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way,b:Drivers should use hand signals to decide who goes first,c:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left yields
note: When two drivers arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first; the vehicle on the left should yield.

question: If another vehicle is about to hit you, what should you do first to warn them?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers only,b:Wave your arms,c:Sound your horn to alert the other driver
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians of imminent danger so they can take evasive action.

question: At what minimum BAC can a driver under 21 be charged with Operating a Vehicle After Underage Consumption in Ohio?
options: a:0.10 percent or higher,b:0.08 percent or higher,c:0.02 percent or higher
note: Drivers under 21 can be charged for underage consumption if their BAC is 0.02 percent or higher (up to 0.08).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a residential area?
options: a:35 miles per hour,b:20 miles per hour,c:25 miles per hour
note: The default residential speed limit is 25 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: Which recommendation does NOT help safe night driving?
options: a:Being aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark,b:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle (not a substitute for safe driving practices),c:Keeping your windshield clean
note: While a flashlight can help in emergencies, it does not improve driving visibility; keep the windshield clean and avoid heavy window tinting for safer night driving.

question: When passing an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road, what should you do?
options: a:Vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle or slow down if you cannot safely move over,b:Stop immediately in the same lane,c:Increase speed to pass quickly
note: Move over a lane if possible; if you cannot safely change lanes, slow down and pass with caution to protect emergency workers.

question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or upset before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drive faster because you'll be more alert,b:Drive as usual since emotions don't affect driving,c:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting
note: Strong emotions can distract you and reduce driving performance; calm yourself and focus before you drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Slightly to the right,b:Toward the curb,c:Sharply away from the curb
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle won't roll into traffic.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving?
options: a:It has no effect unless over the legal limit,b:It can reduce concentration,c:It improves reaction time
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory, reducing driving ability.

question: If you hear a siren coming from behind you while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Stop immediately where you are without signaling,c:Pull over to the right and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass
note: Create a clear path by moving to the right and stopping; in heavy traffic, slowly move as needed to allow the emergency vehicle through.

question: Which children must be secured in an approved child restraint?
options: a:All children only if seated in the front seat,b:All children regardless of age or height without exception,c:Infants and children under age four and/or under 40 pounds
note: Children under age four and/or under 40 pounds must be restrained in an appropriate car seat; booster requirements apply for older children until they meet height requirements.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone on the road,b:Very uncommon,c:Nothing to be concerned about
note: Distracted driving greatly increases the chance of a crash and endangers drivers, passengers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed after a train passes?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing,b:Proceed immediately after the first train passes,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train
note: Do not start across until you can see clearly down all tracks; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving,b:Only watching the vehicle ahead,c:Maintaining eye contact during a passenger conversation
note: An inattentive driver is distracted by off-road sights, daydreaming, or activities inside the vehicle, which reduces safety.

question: During poor weather, what following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Two seconds,b:Three seconds,c:Four to five seconds
note: Increase following distance to four or five seconds in poor weather/traffic conditions to give more time to react.

question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Hot coffee and fresh air will sober them quickly,b:Only the passage of time will reduce impairment,c:Tomato juice and lime will sober them
note: Only time will allow the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce impairment; quick remedies like coffee or fresh air do not eliminate intoxication.

question: Which devices are used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper turning lanes?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road,b:Flashing red lights,c:Lane-use arrows painted or displayed to indicate turning lanes
note: Arrows indicate which lanes are designated for turning or going straight and are used to guide drivers into proper lanes.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation and cultural interest?
options: a:Green,b:Brown,c:Orange
note: Brown signs indicate cultural/historical sites or public recreation areas and are used to guide travelers to those resources.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which locations are specifically unsafe and illegal for passing another vehicle?
options: a:Hills,b:Only intersections,c:Only hills and curves
note: Passing is prohibited on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility and safety are compromised.

question: How can stress influence your driving ability?
options: a:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel immediately,b:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving,c:It decreases your chances of being in an accident
note: Stress can lessen concentration and impair judgment, increasing the risk of mistakes while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are out due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and go through without stopping,b:Park off the road and wait for power to be restored,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn
note: When traffic signals are not functioning, approach the intersection as you would a four-way stop and proceed cautiously when it's your turn.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement's edge, what is the correct recovery technique?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back on,b:Continue with wheels off,c:Slam on the brakes immediately
note: Keep both hands on the wheel, ease off the accelerator to slow, then when safe steer back onto the pavement gradually.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing another vehicle prohibited?
options: a:Both of the above (never pass under these conditions),b:On a hill or in a curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic,c:By using the shoulder of the highway
note: You must not pass on hills, curves, or by driving onto the shoulder; passing in these situations is unsafe and illegal.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet,b:Replace tires that have poor tread,c:Maintain proper tire air pressure
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water rather than the road surface. Reducing your speed on wet roads is the most effective immediate way to lower the risk, though proper tire pressure and good tread also help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to pass another vehicle on the right shoulder?
options: a:When the car ahead is turning right and there is room to pass on the right,b:When the vehicle ahead is driving too slowly,c:Never drive off the pavement onto the shoulder to pass
note: Passing on the right shoulder is prohibited; only pass on the right on the roadway when safe and legal, not by driving off the pavement or onto the shoulder.

question: What type of signs warn you about potentially hazardous road conditions ahead?
options: a:Regulatory signs,b:Information signs,c:Warning signs
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions and should be obeyed for safety.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Exercise to metabolize the alcohol faster,b:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol,c:Drink coffee to sober up
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, exercise, and other quick fixes do not lower BAC.

question: Which effect commonly occurs after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Improved alertness,b:More accurate judgment of speed and distance,c:Slowed reflexes and reaction time
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts judgment of speed and distance.

question: Which substances can impair driving and result in a DUII?
options: a:Only illegal drugs,b:Only alcoholic beverages,c:Any of the above — alcohol
note: A wide range of substances — alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications — can impair driving and lead to DUII charges.

question: Many crashes are caused by which driving behavior?
options: a:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,b:Yielding the right-of-way,c:Traveling too fast for conditions
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a common cause of crashes; always adjust speed for conditions.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:Yes if you are not driving,b:No — consuming or possessing an open alcoholic beverage in a vehicle on public roads is prohibited,c:Yes if you are in the back seat
note: It is unlawful to drink or possess open alcoholic beverages in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of serious injury in a crash?
options: a:Staying in the right lane,b:Limiting driving to weekdays,c:Wearing your seat belt
note: Wearing a properly fastened seat belt is the most effective way to reduce risk of fatality or serious injury in a collision.

question: How can you reduce road rage and aggressive driving incidents?
options: a:Always drive as fast as possible,b:Allow extra travel time so you are less rushed,c:Ignore using turn signals
note: Plan ahead, allow extra travel time, obey speed limits, and use signals to reduce stress and avoid provoking other drivers.

question: A driver extending their left arm downward is signaling what?
options: a:Intention to turn left,b:Intention to slow or stop,c:Intention to turn right
note: When a driver's left arm is extended downward, it signals they plan to slow or stop.

question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle?
options: a:0.02 percent or higher,b:0.05 percent or higher,c:0.08 percent or higher
note: Drivers age 21 or older are illegal to operate a vehicle at a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

question: How can you avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Only turn on your car radio loudly,b:Slow down and keep driving without stopping,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch
note: Schedule regular breaks to rest and stretch to help prevent fatigue on long drives.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the usual speed limit in school zones unless otherwise posted?
options: a:30 mph,b:45 mph,c:20 mph
note: Unless otherwise posted, school zone speed limits are typically 20 mph; always drive cautiously near schools.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down continuously,b:Lightly tap the brakes,c:Firmly pump your brakes
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly while retaining steering control.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Speed up to cut through standing water,b:Maintain good tire tread and proper inflation and reduce speed in the rain,c:Use cruise control to maintain consistent speed
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, ensure tires have adequate tread, proper inflation, and reduce speed when roads are wet.

question: What does a 'No Stopping' sign mean regarding when you may stop your vehicle?
options: a:You may stop only to discharge passengers,b:You may stop briefly to load or unload packages,c:Stop only to obey a traffic signal
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may stop only to obey a traffic signal or officer, or to avoid conflict with other traffic.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what driving effect should you anticipate?
options: a:Wind gusts that may affect your vehicle's direction,b:Decreased air turbulence,c:Loud noises only
note: Large vehicles can create wind gusts that affect smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you carefully continue through an intersection when the light turns yellow?
options: a:If pedestrians are crossing,b:If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane,c:If you are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are already in the intersection, proceed carefully through it; otherwise slow to a stop if you can do so safely.

question: What is the most common color used for general warning signs?
options: a:Red with white markings,b:Green with white markings,c:Yellow with black markings
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering to alert drivers to hazards ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median,b:Continue to the next exit and do not make a last-minute turn,c:Cut across traffic to reach the exit
note: Do not make sudden or illegal maneuvers; proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you pass other vehicles before a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel?
options: a:You may not pass within 100 feet of them,b:You may not pass within 500 feet of them,c:You may not pass within 200 feet of them
note: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, railroad crossing, or intersection.

question: A driver license applicant under what age must have parental or guardian permission to apply for a license?
options: a:Under 21,b:Under 19,c:Under 18
note: If you are under 18 (a minor), your application for an operator's license must be co-signed by a parent or legal guardian in Ohio.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:A sign for public recreation areas,b:A warning about possible or existing hazards ahead,c:A school crossing sign
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about existing or potential driving hazards; they are usually yellow (or orange in work zones).

question: If you are driving in another motorist's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay there to keep pace,b:Maintain a steady speed indefinitely,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you
note: Avoid staying in another vehicle's blind spot; reposition your car so the other driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: What must you do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk marked by solid white lines?
options: a:Assume vehicles have the right-of-way,b:Give pedestrians the right-of-way and stop if necessary,c:Proceed because pedestrians must yield
note: Marked crosswalks indicate pedestrian crossing areas; drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in the crosswalk.

question: What should you do to ensure safety before backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors only after getting into the driver's seat,b:Honk your horn just before shifting into reverse,c:Walk to the back of the vehicle and check for children or obstacles before getting in
note: Before backing, exit and inspect the area behind your vehicle to check for small children, pets, or objects that might be missed in mirrors.

question: What are the most effective restraints for occupant protection in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt,b:A lap/shoulder belt used with an airbag,c:Only an airbag
note: Wearing both lap/shoulder belts and having airbags provides the best protection in a crash; airbags are supplemental to seat belts.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks at your own risk,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed
note: If a train is near enough to be dangerous, do not attempt to cross the tracks under any circumstances until it has passed and the crossing is clear.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?
options: a:Always drive to the scene to see what happened,b:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived,c:Immediately stop and gather a crowd
note: Do not stop at the scene unless you are involved or unless emergency help has not yet arrived; keep attention on driving and avoid creating additional hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a railroad crossing are you allowed to park?
options: a:Within 50 feet of the crossing,b:Within 75 feet of the crossing,c:Within 100 feet of the crossing
note: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Only park where it is legal and other drivers can clearly see your stopped vehicle.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of you. What is the proper action?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian
note: Always slow down and yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, especially near crosswalks and where children are present.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Brake hard to warn the tailgater,b:Speed up aggressively to create distance,c:If you can
note: If a driver is tailgating you, move over when safe or gradually reduce speed when the road ahead is clear to encourage them to pass; never brake abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:After you have started passing,b:Early enough for other drivers to know your intentions before you change lanes,c:Just as you begin to change lanes
note: Signal with enough lead time so other drivers understand your intentions before you initiate the pass or lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using lights or siren on a two-lane street, what should you do?
options: a:Stop as quickly as possible,b:Clear the road immediately and stop,c:Continue to drive normally
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using lights or siren, you do not need to clear the path; continue driving normally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car ahead of the space you want to enter,b:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately
note: After checking traffic and signaling, stop alongside the vehicle in front of the space before beginning the backing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Keep to the left lane to block passing,b:Maintain your speed and ignore the traffic behind you,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass
note: If you're impeding the normal flow of traffic, you should pull off the roadway when safe to allow others to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway, what must you do?
options: a:Always pass only on the right,b:Watch for oncoming traffic only,c:Ensure the passing lane is clear and signal your lane change
note: Make sure the passing lane is clear, signal early, and complete the pass only when it is safe to do so.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop,b:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears,c:Treat it like a flashing red and proceed with caution
note: A solid red arrow means stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps are important when you need to change lanes?
options: a:Signal just as you begin to move into the lane,b:Only check mirrors,c:Signal
note: Always signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions when stopping?
options: a:Check mirrors only after stopping,b:Always stop abruptly to signal urgency,c:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to slow and applying steady braking
note: Avoid sudden stops; gradually release the accelerator and apply steady braking so drivers behind have time to react.

question: If you have a green light and pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed because you have the green light,b:Honk to warn them to get out of the way,c:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely
note: Yield to pedestrians and allow them to cross safely even if they are crossing against their signal; avoid putting anyone at risk.

question: Why is keeping a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It keeps traffic flowing faster,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations
note: Leaving a buffer of space around your vehicle provides time to recognize and respond to mistakes or hazards caused by other road users.

question: What is the legal status of texting while driving in Ohio?
options: a:Illegal for drivers to text while operating a vehicle,b:Always legal but not recommended,c:A safe activity if done briefly at a stoplight
note: Texting while driving is prohibited in Ohio and is both dangerous and subject to fines and penalties.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They will only receive a warning,b:They are always exempt from citations,c:They can be ticketed
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motorists and may be ticketed for violating traffic laws.

question: What does a solid white center line between lanes indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed,c:Lanes move in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or prohibited
note: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and indicate lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.
